case.pattern_description: The fraud pattern involves three online transactions totaling $1,499.84, each just under $500, within a 7-minute window on a single card. This pattern was found by an agent scanning the transaction window of the card, matching it to two confirmed closed cases that analysts could not attribute to any known fraud typology. The affected card is from region 325 and used an IE 11.0 browser on a desktop device.

sar.narrative: Customer C05560, holder of card C05560-K2, is the subject of this report. Between 2016-12-06 11:16 and 2016-12-06 11:23, 3 transaction(s) totalling $1,499.84 were made on the card online from device profile 'rv:11.0 |  | ie 11.0 for desktop | ': $499.98 (3518540, 2016-12-06 11:16), $499.95 (3518547, 2016-12-06 11:21), $499.91 (3518549, 2016-12-06 11:23). Every amount sat just below $500 and the purchases were placed minutes apart, a pattern consistent with deliberately staying under an authorisation threshold. The activity is suspicious because: 3 online purchases within 7 minutes, each between $400 and $500 ($499.98, $499.95, $499.91; total $1,499.84). It closely resembles earlier confirmed fraud cases CC-4169, CC-4086, CC-3907. The bank has recommended blocking and reissuing the card, placing linked cards under monitoring where applicable, and retaining the transaction, device and investigation records as supporting documentation.

stop_reason: Fraud probability 0.91 is at or above 0.85 with 2 independent pieces of evidence, so the decision is defensible without asking the customer (policy 6).
